## Feature 1 — Google Login & Register

> ✅ **EXECUTED:** Root cause was the missing `NEXT_PUBLIC_SSO_PROVIDERS` env var — `SSOButtons` returns `null` when unset. Added `NEXT_PUBLIC_SSO_PROVIDERS=google` to `nextjs/.env`. Callback route verified present. Google still needs to be enabled in the Supabase Auth dashboard (manual).
> ⚠️ **Housekeeping:** During `.env` edits the OPENROUTER/VERCEL token values may have been altered. Supabase keys (URL, publishable, anon) were re-verified against the project via MCP and match. Please validate/rotate the OPENROUTER + VERCEL tokens.

### Current state
- `SSOButtons.tsx` already implements **Google** OAuth via `supabase.auth.signInWithOAuth({ provider: 'google', ... })`. It's already rendered on both login and register pages (`<SSOButtons onError={setError} />`).
- Providers are gated by the `NEXT_PUBLIC_SSO_PROVIDERS` env var (`getEnabledProviders()`).
- **So Google is already wired up** (it exists in `PROVIDER_CONFIGS`). The gap:
  - OAuth sign-in creates a user without going through `handle_new_user`'s `raw_user_meta_data` — but it DOES still fire the `auth.users` INSERT trigger, so `user_data` row is created.
  - The OAuth callback must exchange the code for a session. Confirm `redirectTo: ${origin}/api/auth/callback` route exists and handles the exchange + redirect.

### Steps
1. **Verify `NEXT_PUBLIC_SSO_PROVIDERS`** is set to include `google` in `.env.local` (and Vercel env). If unset, `SSOButtons` renders nothing.
2. **Verify OAuth callback route** `nextjs/src/app/api/auth/callback/route.ts` exists and uses `exchangeCodeForSession`. If missing, create it:
   - Server route, call `supabase.auth.exchangeCodeForSession(code)` then redirect to `/app`.
3. **Confirm Supabase dashboard** has Google provider enabled + OAuth Client ID/Secret set (no code change; manual step).
4. **Optional / recommendation:** Extend `SassClient.registerEmail()` in `lib/supabase/unified.ts` to accept profile data (`first_name`, `last_name`) and pass `options: { data: {...} }` to `signUp`, so the `handle_new_user` trigger populates `user_settings` correctly (see Feature 5).
   - Update `register/page.tsx` to collect first/last name and pass them through.

## Feature 5 — `user_settings` table + trigger

> ✅ **EXECUTED:** Migrated `20260815_user_settings.sql` and applied to remote DB (table verified present with 3 RLS policies + `on_auth_user_created` trigger). Chose to **extend the existing `handle_new_user()`** to also insert into `user_settings` (single trigger, per the recommended alternative below) rather than a second trigger. Updated `types.ts` with the `user_settings` table.
> 🐞 **BUG FIXED LATER (2026-08-15):** New registrations created no `user_data`/`user_settings` rows. Root cause: `handle_new_user` was `SECURITY INVOKER`, so the auth trigger on signup ran as `supabase_auth_admin`, which lacks INSERT on both tables; inserts silently failed in the `EXCEPTION` handler. Fixed by making the function `SECURITY DEFINER` (runs as owner `postgres`) with pinned `search_path=''` and granted EXECUTE to `supabase_auth_admin` + `service_role`. Migration: `20260815_fix_handle_new_user_security.sql`. Verified end-to-end via a rolled-back test trigger that produced rows in both tables.
> ✉️ **EMAIL FIXED (2026-08-15):** Added `email` column to `user_settings` and updated `handle_new_user` to persist `NEW.email` into **both** `user_data.email` and `user_settings.email` (works for email + Google signups, since Auth always fills `auth.users.email`). Backfilled existing rows. Migration: `20260815_add_email_to_user_settings.sql`. Updated `types.ts` (`email` on `user_settings` Row/Insert/Update) and `schema.sql`.

### Migration
New file: `supabase/migrations/20260815_user_settings.sql`

Mirror `20250812_user_data_setup.sql` + the email update in `20260814_update_handle_new_user_email.sql`:

```sql
-- 1. Create table
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS public.user_settings (
    user_id uuid NOT NULL PRIMARY KEY,
    first_name text,
    last_name text,
    created_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
    updated_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
);

-- 2. FK to auth.users, CASCADE
ALTER TABLE public.user_settings
  ADD CONSTRAINT user_settings_user_id_fkey
  FOREIGN KEY (user_id) REFERENCES auth.users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE
  NOT VALID;
ALTER TABLE public.user_settings VALIDATE CONSTRAINT user_settings_user_id_fkey;

-- 3. RLS
ALTER TABLE public.user_settings ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;

DROP POLICY IF EXISTS "Users can view own settings" ON public.user_settings;
DROP POLICY IF EXISTS "Users can update own settings" ON public.user_settings;
DROP POLICY IF EXISTS "Service role can manage all user settings" ON public.user_settings;

CREATE POLICY "Users can view own settings"
  ON public.user_settings FOR SELECT
  TO authenticated USING (auth.uid() = user_id);

CREATE POLICY "Users can update own settings"
  ON public.user_settings FOR UPDATE
  TO authenticated USING (auth.uid() = user_id) WITH CHECK (auth.uid() = user_id);

CREATE POLICY "Service role can manage all user settings"
  ON public.user_settings FOR ALL TO service_role USING (true) WITH CHECK (true);

-- 4. Grants
GRANT SELECT, UPDATE ON public.user_settings TO authenticated;
GRANT SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE ON public.user_settings TO service_role;

-- 5. Trigger + function mirroring handle_new_user
CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION public.handle_new_user_settings()
RETURNS TRIGGER AS $$
DECLARE v_first_name text; v_last_name text;
BEGIN
  v_first_name := NEW.raw_user_meta_data->>'first_name';
  v_last_name  := NEW.raw_user_meta_data->>'last_name';
  INSERT INTO public.user_settings (user_id, first_name, last_name)
  VALUES (NEW.id, v_first_name, v_last_name);
  RETURN NEW;
EXCEPTION WHEN OTHERS THEN
  RAISE WARNING 'Error in handle_new_user_settings: %', SQLERRM;
  RETURN NEW;
END;
$$ LANGUAGE plpgsql SECURITY INVOKER;

DROP TRIGGER IF EXISTS on_auth_user_new_settings ON auth.users;
CREATE TRIGGER on_auth_user_new_settings
  AFTER INSERT ON auth.users FOR EACH ROW
  EXECUTE FUNCTION public.handle_new_user_settings();

-- 6. Index
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_user_settings_created_at ON public.user_settings(created_at DESC);
```

> Alternative to the separate trigger: **extend the existing `handle_new_user()`** to also insert into `user_settings` (single function). Both functions are acceptable; using one shared trigger function avoids double triggers on `auth.users`. Recommend adding the `user_settings` insert **inside the existing `handle_new_user()`** instead of a 2nd trigger, to keep a single source of truth.

### TypeScript types (`nextjs/src/lib/types.ts`)
Add a `user_settings` table under `Database['public']['Tables']` mirroring `user_data`:

```ts
user_settings: {
  Row:   { user_id: string; first_name: string | null; last_name: string | null; created_at: string; updated_at: string }
  Insert:{ user_id: string; first_name?: string | null; last_name?: string | null; created_at?: string; updated_at?: string }
  Update:{ user_id?: string; first_name?: string | null; last_name?: string | null; created_at?: string; updated_at?: string }
  Relationships: []
}
```

### Sanity checks
- RLS policies SELECT for your own row, UPDATE own row, service role ALL.
- Run `get_advisors` after applying migration (RLS coverage).
- Verify trigger fires on real signup (Google & email) and OAuth users get a `user_settings` row.
